Objective To facilitate development of novel disease-modifying therapies for lysosomal storage disorder (LSDs) characterized by nervous system involvement such as metachromatic leukodystrophy (MLD), molecular markers for monitoring disease progression and therapeutic response are needed. To this end, we sought to identify blood transcripts associated with the progression of MLD. Methods Genome-wide expression analysis was performed in primary T lymphocytes of 24 patients with MLD compared to 24 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Genes associated with MLD were identified, confirmed on a quantitative polymerase chain reaction platform, and replicated in an independent patient cohort. mRNA and protein expression of the prioritized gene family of metallothioneins was evaluated in postmortem patient brains and in mouse models representing 6 other LSDs. Metallothionein expression during disease progression and in response to specific treatment was evaluated in 1 of the tested LSD mouse models. Finally, a set of in vitro studies was planned to dissect the biological functions exerted by this class of molecules. Results Metallothionein genes were significantly overexpressed in T lymphocytes and brain of patients with MLD and generally marked nervous tissue damage in the LSDs here evaluated. Overexpression of metallothioneins correlated with measures of disease progression in mice and patients, whereas their levels decreased in mice upon therapeutic treatment. In vitro studies indicated that metallothionein expression is regulated in response to oxidative stress and inflammation, which are biochemical hallmarks of lysosomal storage diseases. Interpretation Metallothioneins are potential markers of neurologic disease processes and treatment response in LSDs. Lysosomal storage disorders (LSDs) comprise a class of inherited diseases characterized by disruption of normal lysosomal function. Incompletely degraded substrates accumulate, accompanied by cellular dysfunction and death. Neuroinflammation occurs as a reaction to substrate accumulation within microglia and astrocytes or as a response to primary neuronal or oligodendroglial damage. 1 Neuroinflammation is of particular relevance in mediating the neuropathology associated with LSDs. Metachromatic leukodystrophy (MLD; Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man database #250100), a demyelinating LSD caused by mutations in the arylsulfatase A ( ARSA ) gene, 2 is a prototypical example of LSD with progressive accumulation of undegraded sulfatides in the nervous system as well as neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration. MLD is an autosomal recessive disease with an estimated incidence of 1:40,000 to 1:100,000. 3 The disease is classified into late infantile, juvenile, and adult forms according to the age at onset of symptoms. Clinical manifestations, which consist of unrelenting motor and cognitive impairment, progress rapidly and are more severe in the early onset variants, frequently leading to death within the first decade of life. A correlation between MLD phenotype and ARSA mutations has recently been suggested. 4 , 5 Considerable research activity is currently focused on developing strategies to target brain disease in MLD and other LSDs with central nervous system (CNS) involvement. Gene therapy, 6 – 8 enzyme replacement therapy, 9 and small molecular weight compounds are advancing from preclinical to early clinical studies and may enable disease-modifying treatments for these thus far incurable, devastating diseases. Clinical phenotypes and disease progression are highly variable, thus complicating the study of new therapies. Tracking aspects of the complex CNS pathology and their response to novel treatments is particularly challenging. To facilitate therapeutics development, biomarkers of brain disease that can be monitored in support of clinical endpoints would be helpful. Molecular changes have been increasingly appreciated in various neurological diseases in cells outside the nervous system, including in circulating blood cells. 10 – 13 We hypothesized that deciphering the molecular networks progressively perturbed in patients with MLD, and possibly in other LSDs, could highlight novel markers potentially useful for accelerating therapeutics development.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated metallothioneins (MTs) as potential dynamic biomarkers for Metachromatic Leukodystrophy (MLD) and other Lysosomal Storage Diseases (LSDs) with nervous system involvement. It identified significant overexpression of MT genes and proteins, including specific isoforms (MT1A, MT1E, MT2A, MTE, MT1P3-C20ORF127), in T lymphocytes and brain tissue of MLD patients and various LSD mouse models. MT levels correlated with disease progression, nervous tissue damage, oxidative stress, and inflammation, and decreased upon therapeutic treatment. In vitro experiments elucidated that MT expression is regulated in response to proinflammatory and pro-oxidative stimuli and through microglia-astrocyte crosstalk, supporting their role as dynamic markers of disease pathology, progression, and therapeutic response in LSDs.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation (HSCT) and general therapeutic treatments in mouse models, alongside in vitro experimental stimulations.
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation involved normal hematopoietic stem cells from WT donors into globoid cell leukodystrophy (GLD) mice at postnatal day 8, which led to only mild symptoms at 40 days of age, consistent with a positive treatment response; no specific dose-response comparisons were reported for HSCT. General therapeutic treatment in mice resulted in decreased biomarker levels, but specific treatment types, doses, intensity, or duration details were not provided. In vitro studies applied experimental conditions such as 10ng/ml lipopolysaccharide, 100
M H2O2-1mM L-buthionine-sulfoximine, 1mM Trolox, 10
M dexamethasone, and 10% serum from WT and GLD mice to primary cortical astrocytes and astrocyte/microglia cocultures for 6 or 24 hours; these were experimental conditions and not patient treatments.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Metallothioneins (MTs), including isoforms MT1A, MT1E, MT2A, MTE, MT1P3-C20ORF127
analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: T lymphocytes (human blood), brain tissue (human postmortem frontal cortex, mouse models for MLD, GLD, MPSI, MPSIII, SD), Cerebrospinal Fluid (CSF), blood cells (human, mouse), pure mouse astrocyte cultures, astrocyte-microglia cocultures
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Gene Transcript (mRNA expression), Protein Level (protein expression, immunoreactivity, immunoblot)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher in disease states, lower after therapeutic treatment, unchanged in other neurodegenerative diseases
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly overexpressed in T lymphocytes (average 1.6-fold higher, false discovery rate <0.01) and brain (average 25.5-fold higher by qPCR, elevated immunoreactivity in white and gray matter, especially in astrocytes) of MLD patients compared to controls. Overexpression was also observed in brain tissue from other LSD patients (P<0.05 implied) and in mouse models (e.g., GLD mice showed highest levels: Mt1 5.5-fold, Mt2 8.0-fold). Levels correlated with disease progression (Pearson r = 0.617; p = 0.0432 with patient age in late infantile MLD) and dramatically increased from presymptomatic to late symptomatic stages in GLD mice. MT expression was significantly lower (P<0.05 implied) in transplanted GLD mice compared to untreated controls. In vitro, MT expression increased in response to proinflammatory (LPS) and pro-oxidative (H2O2 with glutathione depletion) stimuli, was generally increased by dexamethasone pretreatment, and blocked by Trolox (antioxidant) against oxidative stress. It also increased with microglia-conditioned medium and 10% serum from late-symptomatic GLD mice. No significant change was observed in blood/brain from EAE mice or other human inflammatory/degenerative neurologic diseases, indicating specificity.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Mediates metal homeostasis, detoxification, and protection against cellular oxidative stress and inflammatory responses. Acts as a general marker of nervous tissue damage and a dynamic indicator of disease progression and therapeutic response. Plays a role in microglia-astrocyte crosstalk and mitigating LSD-associated inflammation and oxidative stress.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Metachromatic Leukodystrophy (MLD) disease progression and pathology in human patients and mouse models; various other Lysosomal Storage Disorders (LSDs) with CNS involvement (e.g., GLD, MPSI, MPSIII, SD); therapeutic treatment response (e.g., Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation in GLD mice); progressive disease stages; in vitro investigation of responses to proinflammatory and pro-oxidative stimuli; microglia-astrocyte crosstalk and effects of GLD mouse serum; and specific to LSDs, showing distinction from general neuroinflammatory/neurodegenerative diseases (e.g., multiple sclerosis, Parkinson disease, Huntington disease, EAE mice).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Potential biomarker for monitoring neurologic disease processes, progression, and treatment response in MLD and other LSDs. It indicates nervous tissue damage, CNS involvement, and significant cellular oxidative stress/inflammatory responses. Suggests potential for clinical biomarker assay development in CSF and serves as a specific marker for MLD/LSD-related pathobiology. Correlates with disease modification following treatment and reflects astrocyte activation in neuroinflammatory processes, elucidating mechanistic links in disease pathogenesis.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Brain extracts (GLD mice), Central Nervous System (CNS)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased along the course of the disease in GLD mice; specific increase observed in the LSD setting.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Member of the low-density lipoprotein receptor gene family with endocytic and signal transduction functions; potential mediator of MT effects.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Disease progression in GLD mice, not in EAE mice (used as controls of specificity); Lysosomal Storage Disease (LSD) setting.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with disease progression in GLD mice and potentially involved in the mechanism of MT overexpression, indicating a mechanistic link in disease pathogenesis. Suggests a positive correlation between MT and Lrp2 levels in the CNS, which may help in further elucidating the role of MTs in LSD pathobiology.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Expression remained stable, independently from astrocyte activation.

analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Addition of 10% serum from late-symptomatic GLD mice to WT astrocyte-microglia cocultures.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Used to monitor astrocyte activation; its lack of change suggests that serum-induced MT increase is independent of general astrocyte activation.
